summary.text: Group theory studies groups, algebraic structures that are central to abstract algebra.
Rings, fields and vector spaces can all be seen as groups with additional operations and axioms.
Symmetry groups model crystals, the hydrogen atom and three of the four known fundamental forces, and group theory is also central to public key cryptography.

facts.label: Big classification
facts.value: Finite simple groups were classified over more than 10,000 journal pages

facts.label: Naming
facts.value: Evariste Galois coined the term group

facts.label: Unified
facts.value: The theory of groups was unified starting around 1880

facts.label: Historical sources
facts.value: Number theory, algebraic equations, geometry and analysis

items.prompt: You collect rearrangements of a deck of cards. Doing one after another stays in the collection, and so does undoing any one. What have you built?

options.label: A group acting on the deck
A field of cards
A vector space
A polynomial

items.explain: A collection of permutations closed under composition and inverses is a group acting on the set.

items.prompt: You take every possible rearrangement of n different objects. Which group is that?

options.label: The alternating group
The symmetric group
A matrix group
A Lie group

items.explain: If the collection consists of all permutations of n elements, it is the symmetric group Sₙ.

items.prompt: A chemist wants a mathematical model for the symmetries of a crystal. Which tool is suited?

options.label: Polynomial factoring
Modular clock arithmetic only
Public key encryption
Symmetry groups

items.explain: Physical systems such as crystals may be modelled by symmetry groups, with applications in chemistry and materials science.

items.prompt: Why do groups matter for the impossibility of a general solution in radicals for equations of degree five or higher?

options.label: One group has no proper normal subgroups from degree five up
Groups only come into existence from degree five
Matrix groups cannot be used for high degrees
Radicals always form one single cyclic group

items.explain: The alternating group Aₙ is simple for n ≥ 5, and this fact plays a key role in the impossibility.

items.prompt: What do permutation groups and matrix groups have in common?

options.label: Both act only on finite sets
Both are made of invertible matrices
Both act on a space while preserving its structure
Both have a simple alternating subgroup

items.explain: Both are special cases of transformation groups: a permutation group acts on a set, a matrix group on a vector space.

items.prompt: Mathematicians in the 1800s struggled to sort out Euclidean, hyperbolic and projective geometry. What idea did Klein's Erlangen program offer?

options.label: Count how many dimensions each geometry has
Prove one geometry is the only true one
Classify each geometry by its total area
Use group theory as the organizing principle

items.explain: The Erlangen program proclaimed group theory to be the organizing principle of geometry.
